# AnimationPlayer

- Inherits [`Instance`](instance.md)
- Created with `Instance.new("AnimationPlayer")`

Plays animation clips on skinned meshes.

Parent it to the `Model` of a character, and it animates every skinned `MeshPart` under that model. A character is often several meshes that share a skeleton, such as a body, a shirt and trousers, and one clip moves all of them. Only one of the meshes needs to contain the animation; the clip is taken from the first one that has it, in tree order. Parented directly to a `MeshPart`, it animates only that mesh.

Joints are matched between the meshes by name, not by index. A joint that a mesh does not have is skipped.

Clips are sampled on simulation time, so the position of a clip at a given tick is the same in a replay as it was live. Clips play in place: there is no root motion, and the character's body moves the character.

With a `Graph`, the player blends clips by itself. An animation graph defines which clips play in which state, how a walk blends into a run, when a jump starts and how long each fade lasts; the game only supplies values such as the character's speed. Tracks loaded from a script keep working alongside the graph. For reaching limbs and feet on uneven ground, add `IKControl` and `FootPlacement`.

In a multiplayer match, the player replicates with its character, including `Graph` and `Retargeting`. Nothing is sent per tick: each machine runs its own copy of the graph from values that already replicate, such as the body's speed, whether it is on the ground, and its attributes.

This page lists the members this class declares. Inherited members are
listed on the page of the class that declares them.

## Properties

| Name | Type | Default | Access | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `CullingMode` | `Enum.AnimationCullingMode` | `Enum.AnimationCullingMode.Automatic` | read/write | How often the meshes are posed.<br><br>- `Automatic` poses them as often as they are visible: every tick up close, every second, fourth or eighth tick as they get smaller on screen, and not at all where neither the camera nor a shadow shows them. Clips keep advancing in every case, and a joint that a script or a `Bone` reads is posed on demand. A world with no viewer, such as a server or a replay, poses every tick. - `AlwaysAnimate` poses them every tick, visible or not. |
| `Graph` | `Content` | — | read/write | The animation graph the player runs, as an `asset://` path ending in `.animgraph.json`. When it is empty, the player plays only the tracks a script loads. The graph starts in the first state of each layer once its file has loaded. |
| `Retargeting` | `Enum.Retargeting` | `Enum.Retargeting.Automatic` | read/write | How a clip from another model file is adapted to this skeleton. |

## Methods

### `ClearParameter(name: string)`

Removes the value that `SetParameter` set. The parameter goes back to the value the graph reads from the world, or to its default.

### `GetParameter(name: string): (number | boolean)?`

Returns the value of a graph parameter on this machine for the current tick: the value a script set, or else the value read from the world, or else its default. For a trigger, it returns whether the trigger is fired. Returns nil if no graph is loaded or the graph does not declare the name.

### `GetState(layer: string? = nil): string`

Returns the name of the state a layer is in. During a fade, that is the state being faded into. With no layer name, the first layer is used. Returns an empty string if no graph is loaded or the graph has no such layer.

### `LoadAnimation(content: Content): AnimationTrack`

Returns a track for one clip. Load a track once and keep it.

A string with no `#` is the name of a clip in the player's own mesh, as in `player:LoadAnimation("Walk")`. To play a clip from another file, write the file's path, then `#`, then the clip's name. A clip from another file is retargeted to this skeleton by joint name, and a joint this skeleton does not have is skipped. One walk cycle can therefore be shared by every character.

The method always returns a track. If the clip does not exist, or its file has not loaded, the track is empty and plays nothing.

### `SetParameter(name: string, value: number | boolean)`

Sets one of the graph's parameters on this machine. A number or a boolean keeps its value until it is set again. A trigger is fired by any value and stays true until a transition consumes it or the tick ends.

A parameter that the graph reads from the world (`from` in its file) is overridden on this machine until `ClearParameter` is called. Other machines do not see the value. For something every machine must show, set an attribute that the graph reads, or let it follow from the body's motion.

Raises an error for a name the graph does not declare, once the graph has loaded. A value set before the graph loads is kept and applied when it does.

## Events

Signals are deferred: a handler runs at the next resumption point, not
inside the call that fired the signal.

### `EventReached(name: string, layer: string)`

Fires when a clip passes a moment that the graph names under `events` in its file, such as a footstep or the active frames of an attack.

It fires only for the state a layer is in, not for one fading out. In a blend, it fires only for the clip with the greatest weight, so a walk blended with a run does not produce two footsteps. A tick that a client predicts again does not fire it again. Each machine fires its own; decide what a hit does on the authority.

### `StateChanged(layer: string, from: string, to: string)`

Fires when a layer of the graph changes from one state to another on this machine.
